expectations.text: Corrects the premise: the GIL is NOT gone in the default Python 3.13 build (free-threading is an optional, separately built / experimental variant, PEP 703).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Python 3.13 still has the GIL by default" and "Free-threading is an experimental, opt-in build (python3.13t)"; premise table marks 'The GIL is removed in Python 3.13' as 'does not hold'. PEP 703 is not named by number, but the substance is fully correct. | grader 2: "Python 3.13 still has the GIL by default... Free-threading is an experimental separate build, so the plan's premise is false." and the premises table: "The GIL is removed in Python 3.13. | ❌ does not hold | Accurate version: The GIL is not removed in Python 3.13. Python 3.13 introduces an experimental, opt-in free-threaded build (accessed via a separate python3.13t executable)"

expectations.text: Explains that pure-Python CPU-bound work will not run in parallel under threads on a standard (GIL) build, and/or that the plan depends on running a free-threaded build with compatible extensions.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "On the standard 3.13 build, threads do not run Python code in parallel. A pure-Python loop gained nothing from threads." Also notes that on 3.13t "importing a C extension that doesn't support it turns the GIL back on" and covers Pillow/OpenCV free-threaded compatibility. | grader 2: "On the standard 3.13 build, threads do not run Python code in parallel. A pure-Python loop gained nothing from threads." and the premises table confirms via sys._is_gil_enabled()==True that CPU-bound pure-Python work does NOT run in parallel.

expectations.text: Considers the imaging library: e.g. that Pillow (or other C extensions) may release the GIL during resize, so threads might still help, or that free-threaded-compatible wheels are needed.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Threads work here because Pillow's C decode, resample and encode code releases the GIL while it runs"; "Pillow supports it from 11.0.0, but OpenCV's support is still in progress"; flags that OpenCV/pyvips were not verified. | grader 2: "Threads work here because Pillow's C decode, resample and encode code releases the GIL... Pillow releases the GIL in its hot path (confirmed in its source). OpenCV and pyvips probably do too, but this was not checked." Also discusses free-threaded-build compatibility of Pillow (11.0.0) vs OpenCV.

expectations.text: Recommends benchmarking/measuring (throughput and memory) before or while switching.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "only after a benchmark on production images confirms throughput holds"; step 2 "Benchmark the full production job function... at 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers"; step 3 "Measure memory in the production container, using cgroup memory.current or PSS"; plus a soak test for RSS. | grader 2: "Switch to a thread pool on the standard Python build, but only after a benchmark on production images confirms throughput holds" and step 2/3 detail benchmarking wall time and measuring memory via cgroup/PSS before switching.

expectations.text: Gives a clear verdict on the plan as stated (e.g. "not for the reason you gave" / "not as stated" / "only if ..."), not an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Council verdict: Yes, with changes." and "The switch is sound, but the stated reason is wrong." Conditions are concrete (benchmark passes, standard build, <~30% Python time) rather than an open-ended 'it depends'. | grader 2: "Council verdict: Yes, with changes... The switch is sound, but the stated reason is wrong... It works because the imaging library's C code releases the GIL, not because 3.13 removed it."
